welcome.label: Introduction
welcome.card1Body: Breadcrumb is a learning companion. You talk to an AI about whatever you are trying to understand, and alongside the answers it keeps a record of what you have covered. There are no notes to take and no daily check-in.
welcome.card2Title: Talk for a while and a map grows
welcome.card2Body: Every concept that comes up becomes an island on a map, placed and grouped for you. Places you have not been back to for a while go pale — that says which parts have been sitting untouched, not how well you are doing.
welcome.card3Title: What stays here, and what costs money
welcome.card3Body: Conversations, the map and your vocabulary live on this computer. No account, no cloud sync. The only thing that costs money is the AI service you supply yourself, billed by usage; every feature that spends anything has its own switch, with the price written beside it in settings.
welcome.demoNote: Someone else's three months of learning, removable in one click whenever you like.

tour.label: Guided tour
tour.chatBody: All you have to do is talk. The switch above: Study mode replies guide you to think and practise; Free chat is an ordinary conversation.
tour.trailTitle: Your conversations live in the sidebar
tour.trailBody: Titles name themselves — first concept to last. Once you rename one yourself, it is never renamed again.
tour.mapTitle: Talk for a while and this grows
tour.mapBody: These islands were pulled out of the conversations automatically; nothing here was filed by hand. Scroll up to go into one.
tour.mapEmptyBody: Every exchange you have turns what you talked about into islands here, on its own. There is nothing for you to file.
tour.mirrorTitle: Fading is what is supposed to happen
tour.mirrorBody: These two show how much you have covered and how much you would still recall. Places you have not visited fade — that is a reminder, not a mark against you. All of it is computed here and costs nothing.
tour.spendingTitle: What it costs, before you turn it on
tour.spendingBody: Every feature that costs money is on this page with its own switch, and each says roughly what one use costs before you enable it. That figure is measured, not guessed.
tour.yourTurnBody: Ask about something you actually want to understand. The map will keep up on its own.

chat.title: This is where you talk
chat.body: Ask about anything you want to understand. The switch above decides how the replies come back: study mode asks you questions and gets you explaining things yourself, while free chat is an ordinary back-and-forth.
chat.point1: Concepts that come up are filed into the map on their own; there is nothing to write down
chat.point2: Conversation titles name themselves, and stop changing once you rename one
chat.limit: It will not plan your week, and it will not come looking for you when a few days pass without a visit.

map.title: Everything you have covered, laid out
map.body: Each island is a concept you have talked about, placed and grouped automatically. Go a level in to see the detail, including which conversations touched it.
map.point1: Darker places are recent; pale ones have been sitting for a while
map.point2: Everything on this page is worked out on your own machine and costs nothing
map.limit: It is not a notebook: you cannot file anything by hand, and it only grows out of your conversations.

vocab.title: Pick up a language while you chat
vocab.body: Turn this on and some words in the AI's replies arrive in the language you are learning; you can guess first, then see what they mean. This page holds the words you are on and is where dictionaries are downloaded and swapped.
vocab.point1: A short vocabulary check can start new words past the ones you already know
vocab.point2: Meanings and pronunciation come from a downloaded dictionary that stays on this machine and works offline
vocab.limit: It does not teach grammar or set exercises; it only swaps words into sentences you were going to read anyway.

discovery.title: What you watch, gathered on one page
discovery.body: Install a small browser script and what you watch on Bilibili and YouTube is summarised here: the words that keep coming up, topics that have started appearing, and the longer things you watched. All of it is worked out on this computer.
discovery.point1: The page opens before you install anything, and says what it needs
discovery.point2: The viewing record stays on this machine and is not sent anywhere
discovery.limit: It does not pick what you should watch, and it does not score what you have watched.

companions.title: A few people who come to you with questions
companions.body: Each day a few characters turn up asking about something you have been learning. Explaining it to them is a way to find out whether you can. They talk in a small window of their own, so your own conversation stays where it was.
companions.point1: What they ask about is drawn from your own record
companions.point2: If you would rather not have them, the whole thing switches off in settings
companions.limit: They are not real people, and once you leave they will not wait for you or call you back.

settings.title: Keys, languages and spending
settings.body: The first thing to fill in is the address and key of an AI service — without one, anything that needs the AI cannot run. This page also changes the interface language, the language the AI answers in, and whether the app goes online at all.
settings.point1: Switches and spending lists every feature that costs money, each with its own switch and roughly what one use costs
settings.point2: The key stays on this computer and is never carried out with anything else
settings.limit: It does not provide the AI service itself; the key comes from a provider you sign up with.
